tob-10102: Johann Arndt’s seventeenth-century devotional work taught generations of Lutherans what faith should look like in daily life. It urges Christians to move beyond mere churchgoing toward genuine inner renewal, repentance, and love of neighbor. Enormously popular in its day, the book became one of the founding texts of German Pietism, the movement stressing heartfelt personal religion.
tob-10802: Charles Squire’s survey gathers the gods, heroes, and fairy lore of Britain and Ireland into one readable volume. He retells the tales of the Tuatha Dé Danann, King Arthur’s court, and the Welsh Mabinogion, showing how Celtic myth survived into modern folklore. The book remains a handy gateway to the mythology of the British Isles.
tob-4002: Niccolò Machiavelli’s ruthless little handbook advises rulers how to gain and keep power — by force when needed, by cunning always. Written in 1513 after the author fell from favor in Florence, it shocked readers by cutting politics loose from morals. Few books have been more quoted, more damned, or more powerful.
tob-0202: The Kybalion packs the Hermetic teaching into seven tight laws — mind over matter, as above so below, rhythm, polarity, and the rest. The Three Initiates set it down in 1908 for the plain reader, and it became the handbook of the occult rebirth. Its maxims still line New Age shelves everywhere.
tob-3002: Saint Augustine’s Confessions is the first true life-story in Western letters — the tale of a brilliant sinner’s long road to God. He bares his young lusts, his Manichean years, and the garden hour in Milan when a child’s voice cried ‘take up and read.’ E. B. Pusey’s Englishing carries its burning heart across.
tob-0102: Abraham of Worms’s Holy Magic tells how the mage Abramelin schooled him in the sacred art — eighteen months of prayer and cleansing to win the Knowing and Talk of the Holy Warden Angel. This first book lays out the system. It grew into the wonder-workers’ bible from Mathers to Crowley.
tob-4102: Kenneth Saunders’s Way of Virtue turns the Dhammapada — the Buddha’s most-quoted verses on mind, deed, and the good life — into flowing English. His rendering courted the common reader, not the scholar. The book first led many westerners to Buddhist right-living.
tob-9102: Griffith’s Sama Veda turns the chant-Veda — Rig-hymns set to song for the Soma offering. His toil crowned his great threefold Veda-rendering. Priests sang these strains at the Soma-pressing, oldest of rites. The volume keeps olden Hindu worship’s holy-heart, sung these three thousand years.
tob-10402: Athanasius’s Against the Arians defends the Nicene faith — the great fourth-century fight over whether Christ is truly God. The bishop of Alexandria’s speeches crushed the Arian party at Nicaea and after. His case defined the orthodox creed. The work is a pillar of early church teaching.
tob-14502: Rumi’s Masnavi — the Mathnawi — is the great Persian Sufi epic, six books of tales and teachings in rhyming couplets. Called the ‘Quran in Persian,’ it is the masterpiece of Islamic mysticism. The work has guided Sufi seekers for seven centuries.
cia-0000107402: A September 1989 report on Pakistan's defense industry and its struggle to become self-sufficient in weapons production. Pakistan wanted to build its own arms rather than depend on foreign suppliers, a hard climb for a developing economy. The document reflects American interest in how a frontline Cold War ally armed itself.
cia-0000119202: A February 1971 document, source deleted, on reward leaflets offering payment for information on American POWs in Laos. The U.S. dropped leaflets promising cash to anyone who could help find missing airmen. The entry shows the search for the missing reaching into the jungle by paper and promise.
cia-0000124302: A January 1958 compilation of orbital data on Soviet Sputniks I, II, and III. Three satellites, three orbits, three sets of numbers — the raw material of space intelligence. The document is the space race reduced to mathematics: altitude, period, and inclination, telling their quiet story.
cia-0000132302: Situation Report 612 on Iraqi ground forces — the truncated title cuts off their status. The world's fourth-largest army was about to meet the coalition's armor. The entry assesses the force on the eve of its destruction.
cia-0000132402: A January 1961 briefing on Cuba by the Director of Central Intelligence — the truncated title suggests the occasion. The DCI himself carried the Cuba brief: the invasion plan, the odds, the stakes. The entry is the Bay of Pigs, briefed at the highest level.
cia-0000132502: A February 1961 report on Argentina sending special envoys to the United States and Cuba. Buenos Aires was playing mediator — or playing both sides. The document is diplomacy's middle path: the envoys, dispatched.
cia-0000132602: Item 16 in the August 1960 series: a large bloc arms delivery to Cuba. The weapons were arriving — the island's arsenal, growing. The document is the shipment, noted: the guns, landed.
cia-0000135602: An estimated 1961 Spanish-language 2506 Brigade document. The brigade's papers, after the failed invasion — defeat, in Spanish. The document is the aftermath: the exiles, accounting.
cia-0000136302: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN to CADICK on the necessity for early decisive action — the truncated title cuts off in where. The push for speed. The document is the necessity: the action, urged — early and decisive.
cia-0000137002: A 1954 cable to the chief of station in Guatemala suggesting junta action following the junta — the truncated title trails off. The post-coup order, proposed. The document is the suggestion: the action, advised.
cia-0000140402: A 1954 document on the military application of hypnotism — the archive's spelling doubles the error. The mind-control file. The entry is the study: the hypnosis, weaponized — through typos.
un-sc-res-102: Security Council Resolution 102, adopted in 1953. The Council's business rolled on. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-302: Security Council Resolution 302, adopted in 1971. The deliberations continued. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-402: Security Council Resolution 402, adopted in 1981 — this one aligns. The early-eighties Council deciding. The designation and year are certain; the subject belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1302: Security Council Resolution 1302, cataloged with the year 1995 — the numbering belongs to 2000, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-2202: Security Council Resolution 2202, cataloged with the year 2014 — the historical record places this Minsk II endorsement in February 2015, backing the Ukraine ceasefire deal. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000135702: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135702. The invaders wrote in Spanish; the files remember. The document is the memory: the language, theirs.
cia-0000136702: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136702, date approximate. The circa set. The document is the circa: the year, about 1961.
plos-pone-0000002: A 2006 PLOS ONE study on the allometric scaling of the active hematopoietic stem cell pool across mammals — how the blood-making stem cell supply scales with body size. Mouse to elephant, the math holds. The paper is the scaling: the stem cells, proportioned.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d102: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 8, 1943 — Document 102. Washington to Moscow. The message is the letter: the president, to the marshal.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d202: The Acting Secretary of State Stettinius to the ambassador in the Soviet Union — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 202. The stand-in wrote Moscow's envoy. The memo is the envoy: Harriman, instructed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d302: The Secretary of State to the President, November 24, 1943 — Document 302. The department briefed the White House. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d402: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, December 1, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 402. December opened with London's letter. The message is December's: the prime minister, writing.
mysteries-of-paris-volume-02: Sue's Paris saga continues as Prince Rodolphe's mission through the city's underworld deepens. New villains emerge, new innocents need rescuing, and the secrets of the powerful begin to surface. The serial's blend of melodrama and social conscience kept all of France — from workers to the king — waiting for each installment.
life-of-edward-earl-of-clarendon-volume-: Henry Craik's life of Edward Hyde, Earl of Clarendon, goes on through his high years of power as lord chancellor and his sad fall from grace. Royalist, statesman, and writer of a great history of the civil wars, he was among the chief men of his age. A full Victorian life, told with care.
voyages-of-samuel-de-champlain-volume-02: Champlain's journals continue in this second volume, carrying his explorations deeper into the Canadian interior. Encounters with Indigenous nations, the founding of settlements, and the hardships of the new world fill these firsthand pages. An irreplaceable record of the birth of New France.
the-adventures-of-ferdinand-count-fathom: The second volume continues Count Fathom's career of deception through the gaming tables and drawing rooms of Europe. Smollett piles incident upon incident as his villain's luck begins to turn. The author's grim delight in exposing human knavery has rarely been sharper.
the-thirty-years-war-volume-02: Schiller's history continues through the war's middle years, as Denmark and Sweden enter the German conflict and Wallenstein rises to power. The narrative sweeps across battlefields and courts with epic breadth. A master storyteller's account of one of history's most terrible wars.
history-of-the-revolt-of-the-netherlands: Volume two deepens Schiller's account of the Netherlands' fight for freedom, covering the Duke of Alva's terror and the Dutch resistance. Atrocity and heroism alternate in a narrative of a nation forged in fire. The historian-dramatist at his most powerful.
the-prince-of-india-or-why-constantinopl: Lew Wallace's epic continues through the siege and fall of Constantinople, as the Prince of India's mysterious destiny unfolds amid the city's last stand. Byzantine glory and Ottoman power collide in the climax of one of the nineteenth century's great historical novels.
darwiniana-essays-volume-02: Thomas Henry Huxley — Darwin's bulldog — continues his defense of evolution in this second volume of essays. With razor logic and splendid rhetoric, he takes on critics of the new science. These are the writings that won the Victorian battle for Darwin.
the-antiquary-volume-02: The Antiquary ends happily as Oldbuck's puzzles come undone — the heir found, the hoard dug up, the good beggar proved true. Scott winds up his most warm-hearted novel with art and joy. A fine close to a book readers have loved for two hundred years.
rob-roy-volume-02: Scott's great Highland novel rolls on as Frank Osbaldistone falls deeper into the world of Rob Roy MacGregor — cattle raids, clan feuds, and the wild beauty of the North. This second volume brings the tale toward its rousing close. Adventure and history woven by a master hand.
arxiv-2605-08902: Small vision-language models are cheap to run but lag their giant cousins in performance. Mengyuan Tian, Qiyan Zhao, Yanan He, and Da-Han Wang propose DAPE, which aligns visual and textual features dynamically and non-uniformly, then progressively enhances detail. The 2026 paper aims to close the performance gap for efficient visual language models.
arxiv-2605-09202: Block diagonalization splits big matrices into independent chunks, and the SVD-flavored joint version is widely used. Ren-Cang Li, Li Wang, and Mei Yang solve it with an NPDo approach — optimization on the Stiefel manifold done right. The 2026 paper is numerical linear algebra with convergence to prove it.
arxiv-2605-09302: Sampling from a posterior over discrete choices — which design, which drug — is harder than in continuous space. Chaitanya Amballa, Sattwik Basu, Jorge Vančo Sampedro, and colleagues adapt Langevin dynamics, the physicist's sampler, to the discrete world. The 2026 paper is Bayesian computation for discrete decisions.
arxiv-2605-09502: Chain-of-thought traces sometimes reveal the model knows it erred — hidden error awareness. Aojie Yuan, Zhiyuan Julian Su, Haiyue Zhang, and colleagues argue the signal is diagnostic, not causal: it betrays the error without causing the fix. The 2026 paper is interpretability with a careful distinction.
arxiv-2605-09702: LLM judges are noisy — curating their labels by hand is expensive, while calibrating them statistically is cheap. Yanran Li argues for calibration over curation in label-efficient estimation from noisy judges. The 2026 paper squeezes reliable truth from noisy evaluators efficiently.
plos-pone-0003402: Epidemiologists asked how much genes matter for disability retirement in this 2008 Finnish study. Tracking about 24,000 twins for 30 years, they measured how strongly the tendency to retire early on disability runs in families. The results teased apart genetic from environmental contributions, informing how societies think about work ability and welfare policy.
plos-pone-0003502: Neuroscientists scanned brains wielding tools in this 2008 imaging study. Using a tool extends the brain's reach, forcing it to merge what the eyes see far away with what the hand feels, and functional MRI revealed how attention networks handle that multisensory split. The work maps the neural choreography behind one of humanity's defining skills.
plos-pone-0003602: Extinction researchers Wyatt, Campos, and Gilbert blamed introduced disease for an island die-off in this 2008 paper. The historical disappearance of Christmas Island's native mammals correlated with newly arrived infectious diseases. Ancient DNA evidence makes the case that pathogens, not just habitat loss, can erase a fauna.
plos-pone-0003702: In 2008, Gu, Liu, and Guise studied people who struggle to name feelings. Adults with the alexithymic trait, a blind spot for their own emotions, were tested on voluntary control of attention. The work probes how a trait that numbs emotional insight also shapes the mind's steering.
plos-pone-0003802: Managbanag, Witten, and Bonchev hunted longevity genes by network shortcuts in this 2008 paper. Their shortest-path analysis of gene networks flagged candidates that modulate lifespan. The network approach offers a new compass for aging research beyond single-gene hunts.
plos-pone-0003902: In 2008, Thomas, Holland, and Minot tracked an elephant cow for five years. GPS satellite data mapped her home range across Sabi Sand Reserve and Kruger National Park. The long tracking record shows how one elephant uses two famous wild spaces.
plos-pone-0004002: In 2008, Vitorino, Margos, and Feil mapped a Lyme germ's family geography. Multilocus sequence typing revealed the fine-scale geographic structure of Borrelia lusitaniae. The Mediterranean tick-borne spirochete split into distinct regional populations tied to lizards. The phylogeographic map clarifies how this Lyme-group bacterium spreads across lands.
plos-pone-0004102: In 2008, Hollands, Aziz, and Kansal found a mutation taming a strep toxin. A natural ropB mutation suppressed SpeB expression in M1T1 group A streptococcus. Less SpeB tracked with more invasive human disease. The genetic switch helps explain strep's shifting threat.
plos-pone-0004202: In 2009, Martinand-Mari, Maury, and Rousset found geometry deciding cell fate. In still tissues, cell layout decided life and death. A cell's neighbors voted on its survival. The shape rule simplifies planned death. The finding turns cell death into a local vote.
plos-pone-0004302: In 2009, Zangenehpour, Ghazanfar, and Lewkowicz tested baby monkeys' senses. Infant vervet monkeys matched sights and sounds across senses well. The timing of multisensory skill shifted versus humans. The neat comparison illuminates developmental evolution. The work traces how sensory timing evolves.
plos-pone-0357902: Parkinson’s disease shows in the face long before a clinic visit — slower blinking, flatter expressions. This paper tests whether a simple selfie video, analyzed with AI, can help assess the disease. The system extracts facial features and explains its reasoning, aiming for a cheap, at-home screening tool that could flag Parkinson’s earlier.
plos-pone-0355502: Bangladesh grows two rice seasons — aman and aus — and mapping each matters for food security. This paper estimated their areas using Sentinel-1 radar imagery with machine learning. The satellite-based maps give planners timely crop data regardless of cloud cover.
plos-pone-0357602: Sepsis can shut down the kidneys with terrifying speed — and early warning saves them. This paper used BioBERT-BPNN multimodal clinical data analysis for early recognition of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury. The AI fusion of clinical notes and numbers spots kidney failure sooner than either source alone.
plos-pone-0357402: Opioid recovery desperately needs new tools beyond willpower and existing drugs. The VICTORY study protocol plans a randomized controlled trial of non-invasive brain stimulation — transcranial magnetic stimulation — to reduce opioid use. The planned trial will test whether magnetic pulses to the brain can genuinely aid recovery.
plos-pone-0355902: Glioblastomas recruit pericytes and convert them into cancer-associated fibroblasts that shield the tumor. This paper showed these pericyte-derived CAFs correlate with poor survival and become enriched after chemoradiotherapy. The finding names a treatment-induced enemy — therapy itself helps build the tumor’s defenses.
plos-pone-0355202: Do cholesterol-lowering statins waste away muscle over time? This population-based cohort study examined the association between statin use and longitudinal changes in skeletal muscle mass. The long-term findings give doctors and patients evidence-based reassurance — or well-founded caution.
plos-pone-0356802: Iran is tracking its non-communicable disease risk factors into the future. This protocol establishes the IRAN-STEPS Follow-Up Cohort to study mortality and health outcomes associated with those risk factors, building on the 2021 national survey. The planned cohort will watch a nation’s health evolve.
plos-pone-0357202: Network packets might route best by behaving like particles pushed through force fields. This paper leveraged particle dynamics in force-fields for network packet routing. The physics-inspired approach finds efficient paths through congested networks with elegant mathematics.
plos-pone-0357102: Gestational diabetes screening saves two lives at once — but only if guidelines are followed. This retrospective audit across three Ethiopian public hospitals measured adherence to screening guidelines. The audit’s gaps reveal where the system fails mothers who need screening most.
plos-pone-0355602: Fish farm wastewater is rich in nutrients — and reverse osmosis can recover them as liquid fertilizer. This paper showed the recovered fertilizer exhibits storage stability independent of pasteurization. The finding turns aquaculture effluent from a pollution problem into a stable, valuable product.
plos-pone-0354602: Can animals in zoos and aquariums genuinely help save species in the wild? This paper took stock of whether captive species contribute to biodiversity conservation. The balanced assessment weighs the real conservation wins against the costs and controversies — essential reading as extinction accelerates and captive breeding expands.
plos-pone-0356602: Ginsenosides — ginseng’s active compounds — modulate calcium handling in brain cells under toxic stress. This paper compared their differential effects on Ca2+ regulation in rotenone-treated neuronal and microglial cells. The cell-type-specific findings refine ginseng’s neuroprotective promise with mechanistic precision.
plos-pone-0356202: Doctors don’t need giant AI models if small ones match them. This systematic benchmark showed compact vision models match domain-specific foundation models on several retinal imaging classification tasks. The finding is liberating for clinics: state-of-the-art eye disease detection may run on ordinary hardware after all.
plos-pone-0355402: Standing upright blends vision, touch, and balance — but how much does each sense contribute? This preliminary study disentangled sensory contributions to postural control using sample entropy and neural modeling. The computational dissection reveals the hidden division of labor keeping us vertical.
plos-pone-0356102: Young people are taking on the fossil fuel industry for health equity — but what interventions work? This realist review protocol will synthesize evidence on youth-involved interventions targeting the industry’s practices and products. The planned review asks not just what works, but for whom and in what circumstances.
plos-pone-0356002: Inflammatory bowel disease and osteoporosis — gut and bone — may share genetic bridges. This bioinformatic analysis identified apoptosis-related genes linking the two conditions. The shared genes suggest that treating intestinal inflammation might also protect bones — a connection worth testing clinically.
plos-pone-0355302: Depression may begin in the mouth — via the oral-gut microbiome axis. This mouse model study found dysbiosis of that axis in depression. The findings add a microbial dimension to mood disorders — suggesting the path to the mind might run through the mouth’s bacteria.
plos-pone-0354702: Nanjing Tulou — Fujian’s earthen fortresses — draw tourists seeking living heritage. This social media data analysis examined tourist perceptions and heritage experiences in these traditional villages. The findings reveal what visitors value — and what mass tourism threatens to destroy.
plos-pone-0354802: Children from single-parent families carry disproportionate emotional burdens. This study tested mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for children (MBCT-C) on their internalizing, externalizing, and attention problems. The findings test whether mindfulness can give these children tools their circumstances rarely provide.
europmc-pmc2795202: Everyone knows about gut bacteria, but the mouth has its own fungal community too. This 2010 paper maps the oral mycobiome, the fungi living in healthy people's mouths, using DNA sequencing. The authors catalog which species are normally present. The baseline lets future studies spot when the fungal balance shifts in disease.
europmc-pmc2837402: A tiny RNA puts the brakes on stomach cancer spread in this 2010 study. The authors show miR-218 inhibits invasion and metastasis of gastric cancer by targeting the Robo1 receptor. Restoring the microRNA blocked the cancer's advance. The finding adds a molecular lever against one of the deadliest cancers.
europmc-pmc2851702: Flu vaccine tests lean on a blood gauge: antibody levels that block red-cell clumping. This 2010 paper maps how those levels track true protection against flu, using Bayesian math. The team forged a curve from vaccine trials. The curve lets new vaccines prove worth from blood draws.
europmc-pmc2856202: Hip replacements can be glued in with cement or pressed in bare, and Sweden tracks both. This 2010 paper mines the Swedish Hip Arthroplasty Register to compare cemented and uncemented primary hip replacements. The authors weigh survival of the implants. Their real-world data guides surgeons choosing between the two.
europmc-pmc2890402: Cystic fibrosis lungs host shifting germ crowds, and this 2010 paper maps them by age. The authors profile airway microbiota and pathogen load in age-stratified patients. Their work shows the crowd changes as patients grow. The findings guide age-aware treatment.
europmc-pmc2894102: Gold nanoparticles promise medical uses, but safety comes first. This 2009 paper assesses the in vivo toxicity of gold nanoparticles in animals. The authors test where the particles go and what harm they cause. Their safety data steered medical designs toward safer sizes and doses.
europmc-pmc2914702: Tiny RNAs can drive stomach cancer's defiance of treatment. This 2010 paper shows microRNA-221 and 222 boost gastric tumor growth and radiation resistance by hitting the PTEN gene. The authors reveal a resistance circuit inside cells. Their find flags targets for making tumors respond to therapy again.
europmc-pmc2920902: Traffic fumes may seed asthma in kids. This 2010 study links traffic-related air pollution at home and school to new childhood asthma. The authors track exposures where children live and learn each day. Their finding argues for cleaner routes to school.
europmc-pmc2928802: A yeast pathogen resists drugs through a signaling web. This 2010 paper shows PKC signaling controls drug resistance in Candida albicans via Mkc1, calcineurin, and Hsp90 circuitry. The authors map the web. Their work suggests breaking the circuit to beat resistance.
europmc-pmc2957402: Plant shoots sculpt themselves with auxin flows. This 2010 paper shows PIN1 polarity aligns with microtubule orientation in the shoot tip, coupling morphogenesis to auxin transport. The authors reveal the self-organizing trick. Their work illuminates plant form. Gardeners see the pattern in every leaf spiral.
europmc-pmc2966402: Tiny RNAs in blood might flag breast cancer early. This 2010 pilot study tests circulating miRNAs as potential biomarkers of early stage breast cancer. The authors' small trial shows promise. Their work points to blood-draw screening. A simple blood test could catch tumors sooner.
europmc-pmc3092602: Exercise fights frailty in old age. This 2011 review pools trials of exercise programs for frail elders. The authors confirm real gains in strength and balance. Their work guides elder care. Resistance training helped most, they find. Nursing homes now run group classes.
europmc-pmc6527602: White blood cells must stick, roll, and squeeze through vessel walls to reach infections - and L-selectin choreographs the first steps. This review covers the adhesion molecule found on most circulating leukocytes: how it tethers cells to vessel walls, guides their migration, and even sends signals inward. First described in 1983, it remains a key lever in inflammation research.
europmc-pmc6559702: Children of heavier mothers face higher odds of obesity themselves - but how strong is the link? Pooling studies worldwide, this meta-analysis quantifies the tie between a mother's body mass index and her child's weight. The connection is real and graded, underscoring why supporting healthy weight before and during pregnancy matters for the next generation.
europmc-pmc6566902: Resveratrol - the much-hyped compound in red grapes and wine - does more than trend: it tunes the immune system. This review gathers how the plant molecule dials inflammation up or down across immune cells, with relevance to diabetes, heart disease, and aging. The author separates solid findings from the hype surrounding the famous molecule.
europmc-pmc6591002: Beyond the famous mRNA cap, a subtler RNA tag - m7G - hides inside low-abundance messages and microRNAs. Researchers adapted a chemical method sensitive enough to find it, revealing that the enzyme METTL1 places m7G to help process the let-7 microRNA family. The work opens a new layer of RNA regulation to exploration.
europmc-pmc6602502: Chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes are small but mighty for tracing plant evolution - and they deserve pretty pictures. OGDRAW 1.3.1 draws publication-quality circular maps of organellar genomes, now with an expanded toolkit. Researchers turn raw genome data into clear, colorful figures with a few clicks.
europmc-pmc6678302: Exosomes and their kin - extracellular vesicles - carry molecular messages between cells, and clinics want in. This overview covers their origins, cargo, and purpose, plus how to isolate exosomes reliably. Standardizing isolation is the bottleneck between promise and practice.
europmc-pmc6713402: Flu shots save lives - but only if people get the right one at the right time. This report delivers the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices' seasonal influenza vaccine recommendations: who should be vaccinated and when. The annual guidance is the nation's playbook for flu season.
europmc-pmc6715802: Mammograms save lives - but reading them is grueling, eye-straining work. This study trained a deep learning algorithm to spot breast cancer on screening mammograms, matching expert eyes. The AI second reader could catch cancers humans miss and ease the workload crushing radiology.
europmc-pmc6721602: Mitochondria usually couple fuel-burning to energy production - uncoupling lets the energy leak as heat. This review examines mitochondrial uncoupling as a controller of physiology and disease: metabolism, aging, obesity. The controlled leak, once seen as mere waste, emerges as a regulatory masterstroke.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-102: This 2007 GAO report adds up Washington's help for making electricity — lab grants, tax breaks, and sundry other boosts, from coal to wind to atoms. For the first time lawmakers got one ledger showing every thumb on the scale. The report lets Congress see the full price of the power mix humming through American sockets.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1102: The patent office was drowning in paper in 2007 — and GAO's report says its hiring push could not bail fast enough. Inventors waited years while applications piled up. The findings warn that the backlog was not just a nuisance but a drag on American innovation itself.
gao-gaoreports-b-299702: Data Management Services Joint Venture doubled its July 2007 protest — two case numbers, one data deal — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The venture challenged the agency's award; the call weighs each claim. Joint ventures get joint answers in the protest game.
openalex-w7204486002: Gummy candy with a healthy twist: this study developed a handmade gummy using agar as the gelling agent, store-bought vitamins as the active boost, and ginger powder for natural sweetness and flavor. The authors tested whether the recipe works as a real product. Part food science, part kitchen craft, it explores candy that tries to do some good.
openalex-w4403443402: UTe2 keeps puzzling physicists, most of all when squeezed. This paper studies how pressure rewrites the electron map of this odd superconductor. The authors track several superconducting phases that pop up under squeeze. A study of a crystal that refuses to act normal.
pmc-13456902: This 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis pooled studies on occupational risk factors for suicide — which jobs, work conditions, and exposures raise the risk. Combining many studies gives a sturdier answer than any single survey. The findings matter for workplace mental health policy and prevention programs.
pmc-13429102: In this 2026 aging study, activating the lactate receptor GPR81 reduced hallmarks of cellular senescence and improved muscle function in cell and progeroid (premature-aging) models. Lactate — the exercise byproduct — signals through this receptor to keep cells youthful. The finding suggests an exercise-mimicking drug target.
pmc-13439702: This 2026 genetics paper found sex differences in transcription-associated mutagenesis — mutations caused by the act of reading genes — in the human germline. Sperm and egg precursors mutate differently as genes are transcribed. The finding adds a new layer to how mutations arise between generations.
pmc-13448202: In this 2026 preclinical paper, prelimbic cortex-associated stress sensitization and region-specific mitochondrial adaptations were studied across approaches relevant to PTSD and depression. The brain's stress hub adapts its powerhouses. The mitochondrial angle is novel.
pmc-13421802: A 2026 environmental paper building tools for enhanced waterway surveillance — predicting antimicrobial-resistant E. coli and their genes from an urban river. The river's resistome was modeled. The prediction tools serve public health.
pmc-13422702: A 2026 FoodNet analysis of how diagnostic test type affected Salmonella detection from 2004 to 2024. New tests changed surveillance. The analysis quantifies the shift.
pmc-13635002: This 2026 data paper provided an experimental dataset for system identification of a dual-phase gas-liquid transmembrane pressure system. The data enable modeling. The dataset is the contribution.
pmc-13530602: This 2026 conference poster investigated response shift bias and coping styles after hip arthroscopy. Patients' internal standards changed. The poster explores the psychology.
pmc-13448502: This 2026 conference abstract (MMDA-13) studied the impact of bevacizumab dosing on edema response in radiation necrosis patients. The dosing question was tested. The abstract reports the dose-response.
pmc-13509002: This 2026 spectroscopy paper probed element-specific sensitivity of lanthanoid ions to chiral crystal fields via 4f-4f circular dichroism. The lanthanides' optical response was dissected. The element specificity is the insight.
pmc-13533302: In this 2026 ophthalmology paper, subtype-specific macular microvascular changes in accommodative esotropia were assessed by OCT angiography. The crossed eyes' retinal vessels differed by subtype. The microvascular data are the contribution.
pmc-13518002: A 2026 toxicology case report: yellow granular material in hair — a bedside clue to acetaminophen overdose from cold medication. The visual clue cracked the case. The report teaches the sign.
pmc-13490902: A 2026 study of the antifungal effect of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG against oral candidiasis in diabetic rats. The probiotic fought the thrush. The effect is the finding.
pmc-13491702: This 2026 agricultural paper found soil flooding suppressed Fusarium wilt in watermelon by modulating soil chemistry and microbial richness. The waterlogged soil fought the fungus. The mechanism is the insight.
pmc-13488002: A 2026 surgical paper modifying PICO negative pressure wound therapy application to improve patient experience in hip and knee arthroplasty. The dressing tweak helped patients. The modification is the improvement.
pmc-13482302: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis exploring genetic therapies targeting ALS in animal models. The gene therapies' animal evidence was pooled. The review is the preclinical landscape.
pmc-13456602: A 2026 framework paper on competencies and ethical governance for psychedelic-assisted therapies — a practice-embedded quality-improvement framework. The emerging field's standards were proposed. The framework guides safe practice.
pmc-13433002: In this 2026 herpetology paper, axial regionalization was refined through 3D morphometric sampling strategies on elapid snakes — the backbone of regionalization. The snake spines were morphometrically mapped. The refinement is the method.
pmc-13429802: In this 2026 Delphi consensus, criteria for control and remission of respiratory allergic disease with allergen immunotherapy were established. The experts defined remission. The criteria standardize care.
pmc-13431802: A 2026 neuroscience paper: enhanced mGluR1 function caused motor deficits and region-specific Purkinje cell dysfunction. The overactive receptor broke the cerebellum. The causation is the mechanism.
pmc-13540402: In this 2026 review, antifungal management in hematological malignancy patients was covered — from primary prophylaxis to empirical and diagnosis-driven treatment. The fungal strategy was surveyed. The review guides hematology.
pmc-13426402: A 2026 immunology paper: stiff matrix impaired cytotoxic T lymphocyte function at multiple levels. The rigid environment exhausted the killers. The impairing is the tumor microenvironment insight.
pmc-13462402: A 2026 paper on detection of latent tuberculosis infection in healthcare workers. The occupational TB screening was evaluated. The detection serves worker health.
pmc-13430302: A 2026 letter on zero events, limited precision, and the interpretation of olanzapine safety in diabetic patients receiving cisplatin. The statistical caution was the message. The letter is the methodologic critique.
pmc-13532302: A 2026 food microbiology paper comparing performance of IR Biotyper, Nanopore, and Illumina sequencing to discriminate E. coli strains from poultry. The strain-typing methods were head-to-head. The performance comparison guides the lab.
arxiv-2606-16002: One-class support vector machines learn to spot anomalies by training on normal examples only. This paper breaks that single model into an ensemble — a team — of simpler one-data models and combines their outputs. Published in Pattern Recognition, it aims to make anomaly detection more accurate and easier to understand.
arxiv-2606-16202: Soft things like cloth and dough are notoriously hard to simulate. EgoPhys learns physics models of deformable objects from first-person (egocentric) video — the kind a headset or robot camera records. The learned models generalize to new objects, aiming at robotics and AR researchers who need realistic soft-body prediction from ordinary footage.
arxiv-2606-16302: Flood maps save lives, and radar satellites like Sentinel-1 can see floods through clouds. This paper compares two AI approaches — CNNs and Transformers — for outlining flooded areas in radar imagery, with an emphasis on explainability: showing why the model marked each region. It targets remote-sensing researchers building trustworthy disaster-response tools.
arxiv-2606-16602: Neural networks trained to mimic physics simulations (PDE surrogates) often break when moved from simulation to reality. PhysGuard uses Fisher-guided gradient projection to keep the surrogate faithful to the physics during that sim-to-real jump. It targets researchers deploying AI surrogates for real engineering systems.
